frase_gancho.texto: Jade kings, scribes, and astronomers: the Maya world, alive to this day.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: You leave the Gulf Coast behind and enter the Maya world, which spread across the jungle and plains of southeastern Mexico and Central America. The Maya did not form a single empire, but many city-kingdoms, sometimes allied and sometimes rivals, that shared gods, a calendar, and a writing system. Their writing could record the spoken language, and they carried astronomy and the reckoning of time to astonishing precision. And they did not disappear: today millions of people speak Maya languages. In this hall you will see a king covered in jade, reliefs that tell real stories, a ball game, masks that beg for rain, and replicas of two buildings. We begin by descending into a king’s tomb, where his mask awaits.
